discovery: Quantum simulation of Hubbard models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and co-workers proposed in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model with fully tunable parameters. Bloch and Greiner then observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition (2002), which turned a textbook model of strongly correlated matter into a clean, controllable experiment. This opened the field of analog quantum simulation. Later, Greiner's quantum gas microscope (2009) and Bloch's single-site imaging and control (2010) made it possible to see and manipulate individual atoms in strongly correlated states. With these tools the community has studied antiferromagnetic order and hole dynamics in the Fermi-Hubbard model, many-body localisation and quantum dynamics far from equilibrium. The work connected atomic physics with condensed-matter physics and laid the foundation for today's neutral-atom quantum simulators and quantum processors. It is a new way of doing many-body physics.
